verdict_text:
NO

The merge formula is wrong. The spec requires `out = base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)`, but the artifact instead computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1-base)` then applies `tmp + λ(ft2-tmp)` (task vector 2 taken against `tmp`, not against the unmodified base) — precisely the ordering hazard the "Why it is meaningful" section warns against. Expanding both: the spec gives coefficients `(1-2λ)·base + λ·ft1 + λ·ft2` = `(0.2, 0.4, 0.4)` at λ=0.4, while the artifact gives `(1-λ)²·base + (1-λ)λ·ft1 + λ·ft2` = `(0.36, 0.24, 0.4)` — a materially different result that violates Required result clause 2 and will fail the grader's Frobenius-error check on the 48 merged tensors.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
